title: projectfile v1
description: Schema for the projectfile specification, version 1. See https://projectfile.org/spec/v1. Applies to the in-memory tree resulting from parsing a projectfile.toml, projectfile.yaml, or projectfile.json file. The schema enforces the structural contract (required fields, types, identifier shapes). Semantic SHOULDs and recommended vocabularies (technology tags, OS/arch values, ) are intentionally NOT enforced — see spec §3.4 and §3.7 (peaceful cohabitation).

else.description: A document without includes carries its own identity. One with includes MAY take identity from them; validators check the merged document (spec §4.9).

anyOf.description: YAML/JSON discriminator: $schema must be present and equal the v1 URL (spec §3.4).

TOML discriminator: spec_version must be present and equal '1' (spec §3.4). The schema cannot see the encoding, so validators enforce this branch for .toml files by extension; the #:schema magic comment is an editor hint and does not survive parse.

fragment.description: Field shapes shared by a document and an includes fragment, with nothing required (spec §4.9).

$schema.description: Discriminator for YAML/JSON encodings; pins the specification version. A fragment MAY name the fragment schema instead (spec §4.9).

spec_version.description: Discriminator for TOML encoding; pins the specification version.

kind.description: Schema.org type. Recommended: SoftwareSourceCode, SoftwareApplication, WebApplication.

^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$.description: Top-level single-segment key. May be (a) an unknown reserved key not defined in this revision of Section 4 — accepted and preserved (peaceful cohabitation, §3.7); or (b) the first segment of a nested-mapping extension namespace — its subtree is opaque to this schema and MUST be preserved on round-trip. Dotted-string top-level keys are rejected by additionalProperties:false.

localizedString.description: BCP 47 language-tagged string map. As a shorthand, a bare string is permitted and treated as { und: <string> } (§7).

version.description: Project version in the project's own scheme. SemVer 2.0.0 is RECOMMENDED, not required (spec §4.3).

semverRange.description: SemVer-style range expression. Advisory pattern; consumers should consult the language-native manifest for authoritative resolution.

relativePath.description: Relative path inside project directory; MUST NOT be absolute, contain '..' segments, or include a Windows drive letter.

keyword.description: Bare or namespaced (prefix:value) keyword. See spec §4.6.

isoDate.description: ISO-8601 calendar date string in YYYY-MM-DD form.

repositories.description: Source-control clone endpoints. Each entry has a url (a fragment MAY omit it: its origin entry merges into the including document’s, spec §4.9) and optional type/path/branch; role categorizes it (origin/mirror/archive, open vocab) and the reserved value role=origin marks the canonical entry, issues=true marks the forge used for issue tracking, packages=true the one package registries name as the source. Exactly one entry MUST carry role=origin when count > 1; a sole entry is implicitly origin. At most one entry MAY have issues=true, and at most one packages=true. url accepts any scheme git accepts — https, ssh (git@host:path), git+ssh, etc. The forge landing page is NOT a repositories[] value; it goes in links[type=source-code]. See spec §4.3a.

url.description: Clone endpoint. Any scheme git accepts — not constrained to http(s).

issues.description: True for the repository whose forge issue tracker is the project's canonical bug tracker. At most one entry MAY carry issues = true. When absent on all entries, the origin entry is used.

packages.description: True for the repository that package registries name as the project's source. At most one entry MAY carry packages = true. When absent on all entries, the origin entry is used.

role.description: Open vocabulary; recommended values: origin, mirror, archive. The value origin is reserved: it marks the canonical entry (exactly one when the array has more than one element; the sole element is implicitly origin).

oneOf.description: Sole entry — implicitly origin; no origin-cardinality constraint applies.
Two or more entries — exactly one MUST carry role = origin; at most one MAY have issues = true, and at most one packages = true.

covers.description: What corpus the SPDX expression applies to. 'project' (default) covers the whole source tree; 'additions' covers only original/packaging work in this repository, while bundled upstream software retains its own licensing. See spec §4.4.

file.description: Relative path(s) to license file(s). Single string or sequence of strings. Each path MUST be inside the project directory.

upstream.description: Third-party software the project packages or forks. See spec §4.4b.

license.description: SPDX license expression of the upstream.

copyright.description: Top-level copyright block. Holder identities live under `people` with the `copyright` role; per-person `from` / `to` supply the per-holder date range. See spec §4.4a.

year.description: Default copyright year, applied when a copyright-role person has no `from` date.

person.description: A person entry in `people[]`. Persons only — entities go in `organizations[]`. See spec §4.5.

family-names.description: Family name(s). Multi-part surnames are a single string.

display-name.description: Producer-supplied flat name. Consumers emitting to single-name formats MUST prefer this over any synthesized form. See spec §4.5.2.

from.description: First date this person was associated with the project. For copyright-role entries the year contributes to assembled copyright lines (§4.4a).

to.description: Last date this person was associated with the project. Absent means 'present'.

organization.description: An organization or non-person entity in `organizations[]`. See spec §4.5a.

from.description: First date this organization was associated with the project. For copyright-role entries the year contributes to assembled copyright lines (§4.4a).

to.description: Last date this organization was associated with the project. Absent means 'present'.

handles.description: Platform handles and usernames. Open-vocabulary map from platform name to the handle or identifier on that platform (e.g. 'signal', 'matrix', 'mastodon'). Each value MAY be a string, an array of strings (multiple handles on the same platform), or a map of strings (named sub-keys, e.g. a GPG key with distinct messaging/code fingerprints).

handleValue.description: A single platform handle value. String for the common case, array of strings when a platform has multiple handles, or map of strings for named sub-keys.

linkEntry.description: A typed navigational URL. See spec §4.10.

type.description: URL category. Open vocabulary; consumers MUST NOT reject for unknown types. See spec §4.10 for recommended values.

preferred.description: Marks the canonical entry of its type when more than one entry shares the same type. At most one entry per type MAY carry preferred = true. See spec §4.10.

derived.description: True when this link was auto-generated by a producer (e.g. the projectfile CLI's derive pass). Consumers MUST treat derived and hand-written links identically; the flag exists so producers can track ownership and avoid overwriting user-edited entries. See spec §4.10.

technology.description: Recommended values are listed in spec/technologies.yaml. The vocabulary is non-normative (§4.7) — consumers MUST NOT reject documents for tags outside the recommended list.

browsers.description: Browser targets as Browserslist query strings (§4.8). A flat sequence applies to all environments; a mapping of environment names to query arrays generates per-environment [section] headers in .browserslistrc.

oneOf.description: Relative path or HTTP(S) URL referencing a projectfile document to deep-merge before reading. Resolution is recursive: an included document MAY itself declare includes; relative paths resolve against the including document's directory; cycles MUST be rejected. See spec §4.9.

url.description: HTTP(S) URL of the included document.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the fetched bytes. Consumers MUST reject a mismatch (spec §4.9).

includes.description: Documents to deep-merge into the base document. Later entries win over earlier ones; the base document always wins. Includes resolve recursively; cycles are rejected. See spec §4.9.
